chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the voluntary prayer on Friday, and he said: 'Sixteen rak'ahs before the Asr prayer.'
Then he said: 'And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whatever is added to that is better.''
And he said: 'If a man wishes, he may make of them six rak'ahs in the early part of the day and six rak'ahs in the middle of the day, and pray Dhuhr and pray four with it, then pray Asr.'
ai.seo_question: How many voluntary prayers should be performed on Friday before Asr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the recommended sixteen rak'ahs of voluntary prayer before Asr on Friday, a practice rooted in the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. It highlights the flexibility in timing these prayers—distributing them between mid-morning and mid-afternoon—and underscores the principle of abundance in worship, as cited from Imam Ali (peace be upon him). This specific arrangement reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maximizing spiritual merit during the blessed hours of Friday.
